title: Pi: all subagent runs share session ID `session`, so checkpoints capture the wrong transcript

verdict.rationale: The evidence covers session ID validation hardening (path safety, traversal, glob metacharacters) and the Pi captureTranscript validation. None of it shows anyone chose for all Pi subagent runs to share the ID `session` or for the staged copy to override the shadow archive for them. The collision comes from taking the basename of `session.jsonl`, which was never considered.

rulings.text: Ruling on issue #2160 (Feature request: Goose and Qwen Code agent integrations): we don't add agent integrations to the CLI directly. New agents go through the external agent path first, standalone entire-agent-<name> binaries in https://github.com/entireio/external-agents that talk to the CLI over the external agent protocol. Once an integration is well tested and broadly used, we can consider pulling it into the CLI source tree. Closing as not planned for the CLI itself. [source: gtrrz-victor (CONTRIBUTOR), 2026-08-31, https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/2160#issuecomment-5476033646]

evidence.text:
Give every tree Entire writes to a single os.Root anchor

Entire does filesystem I/O in six trees, and until now each read and write
assembled its own absolute path and handed it to os.ReadFile/os.WriteFile.
Containment was therefore a property each call site had to keep honouring
by hand, and several of them carried comments saying so outright:
PluginDataDir "guarantees ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR always points inside the
managed data subtree", investigate.RunDir noted that "an unvalidated id
would be a path-traversal sink" feeding os.RemoveAll.

Each tree now has one package that owns a shared *os.Root over it, and the
names that reach those roots are relative to them:

  .entire                    entiredir
  git common dir             gitdir
  the working tree           worktreedir
  an agent's session store   agent.SessionStore
  per-user config / cache    userdirs.ConfigRoot / CacheRoot
  managed plugin tree        pluginRoot

The roots memoize through one registry, osroot.Shared, replacing three
separate copies of that map. Directory creation goes through
osroot.MkdirAllNoSymlink, which refuses a component that already exists as
a symlink -- os.Root blocks a symlink that escapes a root but follows one
pointing elsewhere inside it, and an escaping one otherwise surfaces as an
opaque errno far from the cause. entire doctor reports the symlinks that
are already there.

Two anchors are worth calling out because they close a real gap rather
than formalising an existing one. agen

The anchors landed in the previous three commits. This is the tail, and
most of it is one bug wearing several hats: os.Root contains a path
without saying anything about what the path is.

fs.WalkDir takes its walk root's DirEntry from fs.Stat, which follows a
symlink, and only the entries below it from ReadDir, which does not.
Every symlink guard here inspected d.Type() inside the callback, so none
of them covered the root: a symlinked .entire/metadata/<session> was
descended into and its target redacted, committed and pushed.
filepath.Walk lstat'd its root, so this was lost in the conversion, not
absent from the start. osroot.WalkDirNoSymlinks lstats the root and
refuses a symlink at both levels; the two checkpoint metadata walks,
clean's tmp walk and doctor's reporter use it. redact.LoadPacks gets the
same check through fs.ReadLinkFS, which os.Root.FS() implements, so it
keeps its fs.FS-only API and its dependency-free position. A symlinked
.entire is refused rather than followed now, so doctor and CLAUDE.md stop
telling the user that intentional setups keep working.

harden: address PR review — Windows volume + glob-metachar session IDs

Three issues from PR #1365 review:

- ValidateSessionID accepted Windows drive-relative paths ("C:foo"):
  separator-free and not reported absolute by filepath.IsAbs, yet
  filepath.Join drops the base dir on a volume name. Reject ":" (the
  volume separator) — portable and testable; no legitimate session ID
  contains a colon.

- ValidateSessionID accepted glob metacharacters ("*", "?", "["). Session
  IDs are interpolated into filepath.Glob patterns (agent transcript
  lookup in gemini/pi/codex, session-state cleanup), so a "*" could match
  unrelated files. Reject them at the validator choke point.

- StateStore.Clear and ClearSessionState globbed "<sessionID>.*" to find
  files to DELETE. With the permissive validator a session ID of "*"
  would have matched and removed every session's state (DoS/data-loss
  within the state dir). Replace globbing with literal prefix matching so
  deletion can never depend on pattern interpretation, even if a future
  caller skips validation.

Adds regression tests for the drive-relative and glob-metacharacter cases.

Tighten summary provider observability and API shape

Three related cleanups surfaced in PR review:

1. listEnabledSummaryProviders now logs DetectPresence failures at Debug
   before skipping the agent. Previously a broken install (permission
   error on a config dir, etc.) was silently conflated with "not
   installed" — the user saw an incomplete provider list with no trace
   of why.

2. buildSummaryGenerator's settings-load failure is logged at Warn, not
   Debug. This runs on the auto-summarize hot path (post-commit hook);
   a settings load failure silently downgrades the user's configured
   provider to the default, and the previous Debug severity hid that
   from operators.

3. buildSummaryGenerator returns summarize.Generator (interface) instead
   of *summarize.TextGeneratorAdapter (concrete). Returning a concrete
   pointer where callers want an interface invites the classic Go
   nil-interface footgun: a caller holding summarize.Generator that
   wraps a nil *TextGeneratorAdapter is non-nil as an interface but
   panics on use. Nil return now yields a nil interface directly.
